llm.summary: The skill mostly matches its stated social‑media analysis purpose, but there are several inconsistencies and runtime behaviors (process control, launching/killing system processes, and a metadata/env mismatch) that merit caution before installing.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims to perform Douyin/TikTok analysis, title/script generation, product and author analysis — the manifest, SKILL.md, and JS code request TikHub and DeepSeek APIs and include browser/ffmpeg/whisper support, which is coherent. However the registry summary at the top of the package lists no required env vars, while manifest.yaml and README/SKILL.md require TIKHUB_TOKEN and DEEPSEEK_KEY; that metadata mismatch is an incoherence that should be resolved.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions ask you to clone and run the Node script and to set API keys; the script can run a real browser or start Xvfb, spawn chrome, ffmpeg, whisper, and even use pkill/execSync. Those actions are within the advertised feature set (browser scraping, audio/video processing), but they entail system-level effects (starting background Xvfb, killing processes) and running external binaries. The agent's runtime could therefore modify process state on the host — this is expected for the feature but increases risk and should be considered carefully.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided (instruction-only with bundled JS). There is no remote download or installer; code is included directly in the package. This minimizes supply‑chain download risk compared to fetching arbitrary archives.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The manifest legitimately requests two API credentials (TIKHUB_TOKEN and DEEPSEEK_KEY) which match the declared external services. That is proportionate for this functionality. The earlier registry metadata omission of these required env vars is an inconsistency. The script also reads general environment variables for display/desktop detection (DISPLAY, DESKTOP_SESSION) which are normal for browser automation but expose runtime environment state.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always: true and declares it won't modify other skills. It writes analysis outputs to scripts/memory/ (and references a local config.js), which is reasonable for a memory/cache feature. However the skill is permitted to run system commands (pkill, start Xvfb, launch Chromium, ffmpeg, whisper), which gives it significant runtime reach on the host while active — expected for headless browser + media processing but worth flagging.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This package largely does what it says (TikHub data + DeepSeek AI + local browser/media tools) but has a few red flags you should consider before installing:

- Resolve the metadata mismatch: manifest and docs require two API keys (TIKHUB_TOKEN, DEEPSEEK_KEY) even though the registry summary listed none — don't assume it needs no credentials.
- The script will spawn system processes (Chrome/Chromium, Xvfb when headless, ffmpeg, whisper) and even uses pkill/execSync. Run it only on a development/sandbox machine, not on a critical production host.
- It writes analysis files under scripts/memory/ and may create config.js if used; check what is stored there and avoid putting secrets in those files.
- Review the full marketing_hub.js for any uses of child_process exec or execSync that concatenate user input into shell commands (possible command injection). If you can't review, run the skill in an isolated environment (container/VM) and restrict network access to the declared hosts.
- Limit the DeepSeek/TikHub API keys (scopes, rate limits) where possible and avoid using high‑privilege keys. Prefer environment variables over committing keys to disk as the docs recommend.

If you want, I can (a) scan the full marketing_hub.js for patterns that build shell commands from user input, (b) list exact places where the script spawns external commands, or (c) suggest a safe minimal sandbox configuration to run this skill.
